title: Microsoft Teams: AI-generated meeting memory for knowledge retention
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap and supplied Microsoft notice support its rollout account, and Microsoft Learn supports its licensing prerequisites, retention behaviour and documented controls. No blocking factual errors were found; the distinction between Facilitator at release and Copilot later is preserved.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft plans meeting memory that lets Copilot and Facilitator retain meeting insights beyond transcript retention.
claims.quote: allowing Copilot (and Facilitator) to retain key insights from meetings beyond transcript retention periods and when a transcript was not saved.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationales
claims.claim: Meeting memory generation is on by default for each tenant.
claims.quote: AI meeting memory files (.meeting files) will be generated for meetings where Intelligent Recap is turned on. The feature is enabled by default in your organization.

claims.claim: The per-user licensing classification reflects a Copilot-licensed participant prerequisite.
claims.quote: When enabled in the Teams Admin Center, meeting memory is generated for meetings where: 1. Intelligent recap was turned on for the meeting, 2. A Copilot-licensed participant was invited to the meeting

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No additional meeting-memory licence is stated, and additional memory licensing is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting memory" "licensing"; Teams meeting memory additional license storage billing SharePoint Embedded Microsoft 365. Opened the meeting-memory and intelligent-recap guides; no additional memory SKU was stated.

claims.claim: Learn marks meeting memory as preview.
claims.quote: Meeting memory is in preview and only available to organizations in the Teams TAP program.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The documented preview is limited to Teams TAP organisations.
claims.quote: Meeting memory is in preview and only available to organizations in the Teams TAP program.

claims.quote: Meeting memory is stored as a file with the .meeting extension

claims.claim: Meeting memory was formerly called AI meeting archive.
claims.quote: The meeting memory (formerly called AI meeting archive) is an AI-generated artifact

claims.claim: Memory generation requires intelligent recap to be turned on for the meeting.

claims.claim: Memory generation requires a Copilot-licensed participant to have been invited.
claims.quote: A Copilot-licensed participant was invited to the meeting

claims.claim: The file includes meeting metadata such as title, date and invite list.
claims.quote: includes meeting metadata, such as the meeting title, date and invite list

claims.claim: The file contains an AI-generated summary of key insights and discussion.
claims.quote: as well as a summary of the key insights and meeting discussion.

claims.claim: Microsoft states that memory contains no raw transcript excerpts.
claims.quote: No raw user data or transcript excerpts are included in meeting memory, only AI-generated content.

claims.claim: Microsoft states that memory contains no raw user data, only AI-generated content.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Memory files are stored in Teams-owned SharePoint Embedded containers.
claims.quote: Meeting memory is built on SharePoint Embedded and files are stored using Teams-owned Microsoft 365 File Storage Containers, or Containers for short.

claims.claim: Memory is not stored in an individual user's OneDrive.
claims.quote: The memory file is stored within a Teams-owned SharePoint Embedded container rather than a particular user's space

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users cannot directly see, open or access the memory file.
claims.quote: Content in meeting memory is only accessible through Copilot, Facilitator, and other Microsoft AI tools. Users can't open or view the memory file directly.

claims.claim: Learn describes Copilot, Facilitator and other Microsoft AI tools using memory to answer meeting questions.
claims.quote: Copilot, Facilitator, and other Microsoft AI tools use memory to answer questions about the meeting for users who have access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn limits memory access to invitees and people given access by sharing the meeting recap.
claims.quote: Meeting memory is only available to users invited to the meeting and users who are given access by sharing the meeting recap.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The supplied notice restricts memory knowledge to users in the organiser's tenant, excluding external recap recipients from that described access.
claims.quote: Memory knowledge is only shared with users who are in the same tenant as the meeting organizer.

claims.claim: At release, Facilitator will use memory to answer meeting questions.
claims.quote: When the feature is released, Facilitator will use the memory to answer questions about meetings and responses include citations linking to meeting recaps or invites.

claims.claim: The notice places Copilot's use of meeting memory in the future rather than at initial release.
claims.quote: In the future, Copilot will also use the memory to answer questions about meetings.

claims.claim: Responses grounded in memory include citations to the recap or invite.
claims.quote: If AI uses meeting memory to generate a response, the response includes a citation that links to the meeting recap or meeting invite.

claims.claim: Memory files are indexed for search.
claims.quote: Meeting memory files are indexed for search.

claims.claim: Opening a search result for a memory file redirects to the meeting recap or invite.
claims.quote: Opening a memory file from a search point redirects the user to the meeting recap page or meeting invite.

claims.claim: Memory files cannot be moved.
claims.quote: The memory file can't be moved, renamed, or modified.

claims.claim: Memory files cannot be renamed.
claims.quote: The memory file can't be moved, renamed, or modified.

claims.claim: Memory files cannot be modified.
claims.quote: The memory file can't be moved, renamed, or modified.

claims.claim: Memory is not generated for meetings with sensitivity labels that include encryption.
claims.quote: Memory won't be created for meetings with sensitivity labels which include encryption

claims.claim: Memory is not generated for end-to-end encrypted meetings.
claims.quote: Memory won't be created for meetings with sensitivity labels which include encryption, meetings with end-to-end encryption

claims.claim: Memory is not generated for meetings where copying and forwarding are restricted.
claims.quote: or meetings where copying and forwarding content is restricted.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default memory expiration is five years, or 1,825 days.
claims.quote: The default expiration time for memory files is five years (1,825 days)

claims.claim: Administrators can customise default memory expiration in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Default expiration of memory files is controlled through the Teams Admin Center. The default expiration time for memory files is five years (1,825 days), but admins can customize the expiration time as needed for their organization.

claims.claim: Purview retention policies take precedence over the Teams memory expiration setting.
claims.quote: Purview retention policies will take precedence over the meeting memory expiration setting in the Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: Deleting or expiring a transcript or recording does not automatically delete the memory.
claims.quote: Meeting memory won't automatically be deleted if the transcript or recording is deleted or expired.

claims.claim: Organisers can delete memory by deleting recap content.
claims.quote: The meeting organizer can delete meeting memory by deleting the meeting recap. First, navigate to the meeting recap. Then, open the … menu, and select Delete recap content.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A Teams administrator can delete a meeting's memory using the Teams PowerShell connection.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Teams admin can also delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell: 1. Open PowerShell. 2. Run Connect-MicrosoftTeams and sign in with your Teams admin account.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: eDiscovery can search memory through All SharePoint Sites or by specific container URLs.
claims.quote: Admins can perform eDiscovery searches on all SharePoint Embedded content using the All SharePoint Sites workload. Admins can also specify specific meeting memory containers using container URLs.

claims.claim: Memory content supports eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: eDiscovery admins can perform eDiscovery Hold and Export on memory file content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: Memory files do not yet support Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Meeting memory files do not yet support Information Barriers.

claims.claim: MC1429018 was updated on 30 October 2026.
claims.quote: Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice targets control rollout for Targeted Release from early January to mid-January 2027.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Beginning early January 2027 (previously early November 2026) and expected to complete mid-January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026)

claims.claim: The notice targets Worldwide GA control rollout from mid-January to late January 2027.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026) and expected to complete late January 2027 (previously early January)

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The published windows concern controls, with memory generation beginning four weeks after the setting reaches the organisation.
claims.quote: The dates above reflect when admin controls become available. [...] Memory file generation will begin 4 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.

claims.claim: The Meeting memory setting is under Teams admin center meeting policies, with a policy selected for configuration.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Meeting policies. [...] Find the Meeting memory setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy accepts -Identity and the Boolean -AllowMeetingKnowledgeGeneration to control memory generation for the user's meetings.
claims.quote: This setting allows admins to control whether an AI-generated meeting knowledge file is created for meetings organized by the user. [...] Type: Boolean

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The UI offers On for all meetings, Only for meetings with transcription, and Off.
claims.quote: On for all meetings (default): Memory is created for meetings with Intelligent Recap. [...] Only for meetings with transcription: Memory is created for meetings with Intelligent Recap that are transcribed. [...] Off: Memory is turned off for your organization.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference warns that AllowMeetingKnowledgeGeneration has no effect until the feature is released.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: No administrator UI for inspecting and removing individual meeting memories is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory inspect remove generated memory admin center delete recap content UI. Opened the memory guide; it documents an organiser recap-deletion UI and Teams-admin PowerShell, not an administrator UI for this operation.

claims.claim: Get-AIGeneratedKnowledgeContainer -ThreadId <id> finds the memory container URL, with ThreadId required and CallId optional.
claims.quote: A specific memory file container URL can be found by the Teams admin through PowerShell: [...] (ThreadId is required; CallId is optional). [...] Get-AIGeneratedKnowledgeContainer -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String>

claims.where: controls[1].api; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <id> deletes a meeting memory, with ThreadId required and CallId optional.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Teams admin can also delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell: [...] (ThreadId is required; CallId is optional) [...] Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String>

claims.claim: Copilot is configured at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. [...] Select an existing policy or create a new one. [...] Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: The Copilot guide documents Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -Copilot with Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn or Disabled.
claims.quote: On | Enabled [...] On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript [...] On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn [...] Off | Disabled

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference lists only Enabled and EnabledWithTranscript for Copilot, unlike the guide's four values.
claims.quote: Possible values are: - Enabled - EnabledWithTranscript

claims.claim: Retention policies are created at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. [...] Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule supports -Name, -Policy, -RetentionDuration and -RetentionComplianceAction as printed.
claims.quote: New-RetentionComplianceRule -Name InternalCompanyRule -Policy "Internal Company Policy" -RetentionDuration Unlimited -RetentionComplianceAction Keep

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Retention of memory containers can be controlled by an existing policy scoped to their container URLs.
claims.quote: To target memory with a different policy, you can use the include or exclude settings to scope your search to your meeting memory container URLs.

claims.claim: The retention-rule cmdlet is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: An integer RetentionDuration value specifies days.
claims.quote: The RetentionDuration parameter specifies the hold duration for the retention rule. Valid values are: - An integer: The hold duration in days.

claims.claim: The retention rule action values are Keep, Delete and KeepAndDelete.
claims.quote: The RetentionComplianceAction parameter specifies the retention action for the rule. Valid values are: - Delete - Keep - KeepAndDelete

claims.claim: Creating a retention policy requires at least one location parameter.
claims.quote: at least one location parameter must be defined to create a retention policy or retention label policy.

claims.claim: A retention rule must be added to an existing policy, which is not valid as a retention policy until a rule is added.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies).

claims.claim: The meeting-memory guide states that default expiration is configured in the Teams admin center but gives no navigation path for it.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory default expiration Teams admin center navigation setting. Opened the full memory guide and relevant results; its expiration section gives the admin center, not a navigation path. Recap .docx expiration is a different control.

claims.claim: Turning off intelligent recap in a meeting's options stops memory generation for that meeting.
claims.quote: Memory generation can be turned off for a specific meeting by turning off Intelligent Recap in the meeting options.

claims.claim: Deactivating the organiser does not remove meeting memory from its Teams-owned storage.
claims.quote: the meeting memory still exists even if the meeting organizer's account is deactivated. The memory remains until the default expiration time specified in the Teams Admin Center, unless Purview retention policies are set.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot directly manage memory containers with SharePoint Embedded APIs.
claims.quote: Meeting memory containers are fully managed in Microsoft Teams' services. Admins can't directly use SharePoint Embedded APIs to manage meeting memory containers.

claims.claim: Expired and deleted memory cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: When the expiration time is reached, the memory file is deleted and can't be recovered.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap requires a Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: You must assign a Teams Premium license or Microsoft Copilot license to your users.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a customer-visible storage charge or storage billing arrangement specifically for Teams meeting memory.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting memory" "billing"; "meeting memory" "storage" "charges"; SharePoint Embedded first-party billing. Opened memory guide, Embedded overview, choose-billing-model and billing-meters: platform meters are published, but no memory-specific customer billing arrangement.
